title: Spiral Matrix
prompt:
Given an `m x n` matrix, return all of its elements in spiral order (clockwise, starting from the top-left).

**Example**: `[[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9]]` → `[1,2,3,6,9,8,7,4,5]`.

**Constraints**: `1 ≤ m, n ≤ 10`.
hints: Think of the matrix as nested rings. Which four straight passes trace one ring?
Keep four boundaries `top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`. After each pass (right along top, down right, left along bottom, up left), move that boundary inward.
Guard the bottom pass with `if (top <= bottom)` and the left pass with `if (left <= right)`, or a leftover single row or column gets read twice.

solution.explanation: Each loop reads the outer ring of the remaining rectangle and then shrinks it, so every cell is read exactly once. The two guards cover the degenerate case where the remaining rectangle is one row or one column. O(m·n) time, O(1) extra space beyond the output.
